title: Turn uploaded release files into checked launch packages
summary: A developer built StreamForge, where uploading a release file triggers Gemma 3 agents to extract specs, translate copy and price tiers; a reviewer agent fixed a euro rounding error.
agent_role: Three agents work in parallel on specs, localization and revenue forecasts; a critic agent audits and repairs the combined result, and a publisher agent saves the final package. The human uploads the file and designs the pipeline.
outcome: Author reports the critic caught a €459.08 price breaking a German rounding rule, corrected it to €460, and passed on the second check.
what_they_did: A developer wired cloud storage so that uploading a product release file starts a team of agents. One pulls out technical highlights, one writes launch headlines in English, German and Japanese, and one forecasts revenue and regional prices. A reviewer agent then checks everything and loops up to three times to fix problems before the result is saved.
how_it_went: In the walkthrough, the reviewer flagged a German price that wasn't rounded to the nearest €5 and changed it to €460. The second check passed and the package was saved.
worth_knowing: Running the agents in parallel is faster, but the author adds the reviewer step because parallel output can publish unrounded or inconsistent prices.
prompt: When I give you a product release file [file path], extract the key technical highlights, write launch headlines for [target languages/regions], and draft prices for [price tiers] in [currencies]. Then review all three together against these rules: [pricing rules, e.g. round euro prices to nearest €5]. List any problems, fix them, and recheck up to three times. Show me the final launch package and wait for my approval before saving or publishing it.

curation.rationale: A code-backed guide where a file upload triggers agents that extract specs, translate launch copy and check regional pricing, with a reviewer loop fixing a euro price. Mostly an architecture tutorial with a demo scenario.
